page: Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an AWS Graviton processor built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Delivered via the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz. With 1.0 thread per core, the hardware eliminates resource contention common to simultaneous multithreading. Cache architecture features 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance provides 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no GPU hardware.

Benchmark results reflect balanced multi-core execution paired with modest single-thread capacity. Synthetic multi-core evaluations show mid-tier results, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5457.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 12132.72. Software compilation utilizing Clang reaches an average score of 8600.0, and static web serving achieves 9.46 GB/sec throughput. In contrast, single-core processing measures lower, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 960.0 and below-average throughput in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression. LLM inference processing registers in the lower tiers across small model tests.

The 1:2 compute-to-memory configuration offers predictable throughput and operational cost efficiency for parallelized, scale-out workloads. Dedicated ARM cores ensure steady execution metrics without noisy-neighbor interference on core execution pipelines. This hardware profile aligns with multi-threaded CI/CD build environments, containerized microservices, batch compute, and in-memory caching solutions, evidenced by Redis processing benchmarks reaching 9.39 million SET operations per second.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro System. Driven by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the system assigns one dedicated thread per physical core across 8 vCPUs. It features 16.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core, along with 32 MB of shared L3 cache and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistence. Benchmark results indicate steady multi-core execution for software builds, ray tracing, and Redis key-value workloads achieving 9.39 million operations per second, contrasted by modest single-threaded compute and compression throughput. This profile delivers reliable cost efficiency for distributed container deployments, multi-threaded CI/CD pipelines, and web serving clusters.
